scope: 1 Peter 3:1-22 source/evidence + cross-lane integration audit with Agent A blocker rerun
do_not_claim: Do not claim every wife in 3:1-6 had an unbelieving husband; the text says some.
Do not make ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει one settled physical/social/moral sense from morphology.
Do not call 3:10-12 mechanically verbatim Psalm 34; use sustained quotation/adaptation.
Do not make morphology prove the full Christological force of Isaiah 8 reuse.
Do not say the inspected SBLGNT opening clause of 3:18 reads 'died'; it reads ἔπαθεν.
Do not settle σαρκί/πνεύματι, spirits in prison, or ἐκήρυξεν chronology from morphology.
Do not claim direct dependence on 1 Enoch from Watchers/Noah parallels alone.
Do not claim ἐπερώτημα means only pledge or only appeal.
Do not prove or disprove baptismal regeneration by lexical fiat.
Do not claim conservative consensus on 3:19-21.
Do not infer empire-wide official persecution from chapter 3 alone.
source_gaps: Critical apparatus remains required before manuscript-distribution claims at 3:18.
Crawford full article remains required before ranking pledge over appeal.
Metadata/bibliographic commentary records remain card-ineligible until relevant passage inspection.
Location-specific Roman/Asia-Minor legal primary evidence remains required before universal wife-status claims.
Direct literary dependence on 1 Enoch remains unproved.

A: No universal legal/social profile for every wife is warranted.
B: εἰς τοῦτο attachment remains contested; omission motive is unclaimed; broader Psalm role remains scholarly interpretation; Gréaux remains abstract-bounded.
C: Isaiah reuse classification and Christological force remain interpretation; Moyise 2005 is not author-independent from the 2002 coauthored study; metadata-only Jobes/Achtemeier/BDAG remain nonclaim controls.
D: spirits/timing/proclamation, ἐπερώτημα translation, baptism systematics, flesh/spirit force remain disputed/noncompetitive; no production/ranking authorization.
